comparator.name: Spatial Planning and Design
comparator.sourceNotes: The formal 2026–2027 regulations and current programme page agree on a single 180-EC English-taught bachelor: 60 EC in year one, 60 EC in year two, and 30 EC of fixed third-year study plus 30 EC of approved electives, minor, exchange or internship. The 15-EC Bachelor Project is split across semesters 2a and 2b in the TER but retained as one coherent component. The 30-EC third-year choice space is left open rather than populated with arbitrary modules. There is no named internal route to select.
components: Approved third-year choice space retained without arbitrary course selection.
Compulsory individual thesis project, split 5 EC in semester 2a and 10 EC in semester 2b.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Spatial planning, physical and institutional design, urbanism and the built environment
Climate, water, environmental systems, landscapes and physical geography
Planning governance, complex decision-making, economics, law and quality of life
Spatial evidence, GIS, statistics, qualitative and quantitative research
Creative design practice, design standards, studios, research philosophy and independent project work
adjacent: Climate-resilient cities, water systems and environmental planning
Urban systems, infrastructure, governance and institutional planning
questions: How can planning and design improve quality of life while managing competing spatial claims?
How can cities and rural areas adapt to climate, water and environmental pressures?
How can evidence, design thinking and public institutions guide spatial transformation?

alternatives.label: Spatial planning, environment & infrastructure
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines spatial sustainability, water and environmental systems, social-spatial analysis, economics, governance, data and applied research; it approximates planning while acknowledging the absence of professional spatial studios.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines sustainability, water, environmental systems, spatial data, economics, sociology and governance; the label names its planning aim while accurately identifying the strongest visible UCR strands.
progression: Social-science, sustainability, data and research foundations precede water, earth observation, environmental systems, economics, governance and applied landscape research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Climate-resilient cities & environmental systems
alternatives.concept: A distinct environmental-planning direction focused on climate adaptation, water, hazards, earth systems, ecological evidence and resilient urban and regional systems.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by climate, water, hazards, ecology, earth observation, environmental systems and applied sustainability research directed toward resilient places.
progression: Ecology, earth-system, water, climate and data foundations precede soils, hazards, earth observation, environmental systems and advanced applied research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This direction replaces ten courses from the broad planning programme with ecology, hazards, soils, biogeochemistry, resources, machine learning and renewable-system design; it differs by 75 EC.

alternatives.label: Urban governance & institutional planning
alternatives.concept: A distinct institutional-planning direction focused on public governance, law, economics, participation, stakeholder communication and the social consequences of urban transformation.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by sociology, politics, law, economics, participation, communication and sustainability governance directed toward institutional planning questions.
alternatives.distinctness: This direction replaces ten courses from the broad programme with law, constitutional institutions, product design, climate communication, persuasive communication and leadership; it also differs from the climate/environment direction by twenty courses.
progression: Sociology, politics, law, economics and research foundations precede planning governance, public decision-making, rights, stakeholder communication and advanced policy study. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The closest schedule combines spatial sustainability, environmental systems, water, evidence and governance. Climate/environmental planning and urban institutional planning are separately supported by direct programme-interest clusters, produce coherent curricula and differ from each prior schedule by at least ten courses. Production therefore stops at the three-alternative maximum.

blocks: Both make a direct contribution to planning, design and socio-spatial change, although the UCR course remains interdisciplinary rather than professional planning training.

notes.text: Groningen requires dedicated spatial-design and urbanism ateliers, GIS, mobility and infrastructure planning, water planning, environmental engineering and a 15-EC planning thesis. UCR can assemble strong interdisciplinary programmes around sustainability, water, governance, data and social-spatial questions, but it does not reproduce the same professional studio, GIS and engineering sequence.
The comparator’s 30-EC electives/minor/exchange/internship space remains open approved choice and is not filled with arbitrary courses.
